Subject: Can't acknowledge PO — login shows device mismatch

Hi Marissa,

We're trying to acknowledge PO #NW-7421 in the supplier portal this morning but every time our procurement user signs in we get a device-binding error: 'Fingerprint mismatch — session blocked'. I attached a screenshot and a log excerpt from our side.

This started after our IT rolled out a privacy extension to Chrome that strips certain headers. We can still access the portal initially, but any action that requires device binding (accept PO, upload W9) fails with the same message.

Can you confirm if Redwood enforces a device fingerprint attribute on the session? If there's a temporary bypass for this supplier so procurement can accept the PO today that would be ideal — we have a cutover scheduled.

Thanks,
Samira Khan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@nobleworks.io>
Cc: it-support@nobleworks.io
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Can't acknowledge PO — login shows device mismatch

Thanks for the prompt report and logs, Samira. Quick findings from the trace (pulled from your attached nobleworks-debug.log):
- Our gateway looks for an IDP-provided attribute named x-device-fp and hashes it before persisting to the session store.
- In your logs, the attribute is present but empty for POSTs after the extension is active; the cookie fingerprint still exists but the attribute-level header is dropped by the extension.

Short-term mitigations:
1) Use Ben's one-time bypass link — it will skip the x-device-fp enforcement for the session and let you finish the PO acknowledgement.
2) If users can reproduce in a single browser, have them open an incognito window (extensions disabled by default) and try the portal there.

Medium-term fixes (we'll schedule):
- Make the gateway accept fingerprint from cookie if x-device-fp header is missing but cookie is present (fallback behavior).
- Add a tenant-level flag that relaxes enforcement for a configurable window during onboarding.

I've created INF-4421 in our tracker for the fallback work and assigned a small patch. I'll attach a link and keep you updated.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Platform Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@nobleworks.io>

Hi Ben / Marissa — confirming Ben's bypass link worked and we accepted PO #NW-7421. We also tested in an incognito window — that worked too. NobleWorks IT will push a communication to the team to disable the privacy extension for portal tasks while you put the fallback in place.

Thanks for the quick help and the temporary bypass — appreciate the escalation. Please keep INF-4421 on your radar; we don't want this to recur with other suppliers after our security rollouts.

Best,
Samira Khan
